transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, um… I guess the main thing is I haven’t really been eating right the last few weeks. Like, I’ll get off my shift and normally there’s stuff I’d look forward to—nothing fancy, just food I usually like—and lately it just kind of sits there. I take a few bites because I know I should, but I don’t really want it.

It’s weird because at work, you know, sitting there watching monitors for hours, sometimes you think about what you’re gonna eat after, but now even that doesn’t sound good. So… that’s why I came in, I guess.
Have you noticed that you’re not enjoying other things you used to like, not just food?

Yeah… yeah, I guess it’s not just food. I used to run in the mornings before work—nothing serious, just around the neighborhood—and I’d feel pretty good after. Lately I keep finding reasons not to go.

Same with guitar. I’ll see it sitting there and think I should pick it up, but it just feels like… effort. Like a chore. Even cooking dinner, which I used to kind of enjoy, chopping stuff and messing around with spices—now I just don’t care enough to start. It’s kind of strange because those were normal parts of my day, you know?
Have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, for the last couple of weeks?

Yeah… most days, I’d say. It’s not like I’m crying all day or anything, it’s more like this heavy, flat feeling I’m carrying around.

Like even when I’m home with my family, or sitting in the break room at work and people are talking about whatever—sports, schedules, some dumb thing somebody saw online—I’m there, but I don’t really feel there. I just kind of sit with it. It’s been like that a lot lately.
Have you been having trouble sleeping lately, or on the flip side, do you find yourself sleeping more than usual?

I don’t know… I haven’t really paid close attention to it, I guess. I work odd hours sometimes, so sleep is always kind of weird for me anyway. Like, if I’m on monitors late, then I come home and it takes a bit to switch off, but that’s been true for years.

I wouldn’t say I’ve noticed some big change one way or the other. It’s hard to tell what’s sleep and what’s just the schedule, you know?
Have you noticed that you feel tired or like you don’t have much energy lately, even if you’ve had enough rest?

I’m not sure, honestly. I mean, everybody’s tired, right? With my job, sometimes it’s just sitting there watching screens, and somehow that makes you feel drained even though you’re not doing much physically.

But I don’t know if it’s more than usual. Some days I feel kind of wiped out, but then I think, well, maybe I didn’t sleep great or maybe it’s just the schedule. It’s hard for me to separate that out.
Have you been feeling like you’re not good enough, or been blaming yourself for things more than usual lately?

I don’t know… I mean, I get annoyed with myself sometimes, sure. Like if I forget something at work or I say the wrong thing at home, I’ll think about it longer than I probably need to.

But I wouldn’t say I’m walking around thinking I’m some terrible person or anything. It’s more just… I don’t know. Sometimes I second-guess myself. Though honestly, with that job, you’re kind of trained to second-guess everything—watching cameras, checking little details, wondering if you missed something. It gets in your head a bit.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight lately?

Yeah… that’s actually kind of why I ended up coming in. The last few weeks I just haven’t really wanted to eat much. Like after a shift I used to grab something I liked, you know, something easy, but lately it’ll just sit there and I’ll take a few bites because I know I should.

I don’t know about exact weight, I don’t really check the scale much. My work pants maybe feel a little different, but that could be laundry too. I just know the appetite thing’s been off.
Have you noticed any changes in your weight recently, like losing or gaining weight without trying to change your diet or activity level?

I haven’t really weighed myself, so I can’t say for sure if I’ve lost anything. I don’t keep a scale around—last time I had one I’d just shove it under the sink with all the cleaning stuff and forget about it.

But the appetite’s definitely been off. That’s kind of what made me come in. For the last few weeks, food just doesn’t appeal much. Even stuff I usually like after work, I’ll get it and then it just sits there, and I’m kind of forcing myself to take a few bites.
Have you noticed that you've been moving more slowly than usual, or on the flip side, been more restless or fidgety lately?

Yeah… maybe slower, I guess. I didn’t really notice it at first, because at work you’re sitting a lot anyway, watching screens and listening to briefings, and those briefings can drag on forever depending who’s running them.

But a couple people have kind of pointed it out—like I’m taking longer to answer when someone asks me something, or I’m moving slow getting through the briefing stuff. It’s like my body and my mouth are both a step behind everybody else. Not really fidgety, more just… delayed, I guess.
Have you noticed feeling more fatigued or having less energy than usual, even when your workload hasn't changed?

I don’t know… I mean, my job’s kind of the same most days, same monitors, same rounds, same people complaining about the coffee like it’s ever been good. So it’s hard to tell if I’m actually more tired or just bored of the whole routine.

I haven’t really, like, tracked my energy or anything. Some days I feel worn out, but I figured everybody does after sitting under those fluorescent lights all shift. I guess I’m not sure if it’s more than usual.
Have you found that you don’t enjoy or take interest in *anything* lately, even things you used to really like?

Yeah… I guess that’s actually been happening. Like, I used to look forward to going for a run in the morning, even if I complained about it the whole first mile. And I’ve got this guitar at home—nothing fancy, just an old one I’ve had forever—and usually I’d pick it up a bit after work.

Lately I just… don’t. I keep skipping that stuff. Cooking dinner too, which is stupid because I used to kind of enjoy making something decent instead of just eating whatever’s easiest. Now it all feels like a chore, like something I’m supposed to do, not something I care about. Even if I have time, I just can’t seem to make myself want to do it.
Would you say that you’ve been feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, for the last two weeks?

Yeah… most days, I think. It’s not like I’m crying all day or anything. It’s more like this heavy, flat feeling I’m carrying around.

Like I can be home with my family, or sitting in the break room at work while people are talking about whatever game was on or who parked like an idiot again, and I’m there, but I’m not really… there. Just kind of checked out and low. It’s been that way a lot lately.
Would you say that you’ve completely lost interest in things you used to enjoy, like running or playing guitar, to the point where they no longer give you any satisfaction at all?

Completely… I don’t know if I’d say completely, but yeah, it’s pretty close. Like the running thing—I used to actually look forward to getting out in the morning, even if half the time I’d spend it thinking about how my knees aren’t what they used to be. And my neighbor’s dog would always lose its mind when I passed the fence, same exact spot every time, like it had never seen a person before.

But lately I just skip it. Same with the guitar. It’s sitting there, and I know I used to enjoy messing around with it after work, but now it just feels like another thing I’m supposed to do. Cooking too. I used to like making dinner, nothing fancy, but now I just don’t care enough. It all feels like chores, not something that gives me much satisfaction.
Have you noticed that you’ve lost more than 5% of your body weight in the last month without trying to change your diet or activity level?

I haven’t really checked the number, honestly. I mean, my belt maybe feels a little different, but I couldn’t tell you if it’s 5% or whatever.

What I have noticed is I just don’t have much appetite these last few weeks. Like after a shift I’d usually want something I like—there’s this place near work that does decent takeout, nothing special, but I used to look forward to it—and now I’ll get food and it just kind of sits there. I’ll force down a few bites because I know I should eat, but I’m not really hungry.
